info.title: AXT relay interface
info.summary: The HTTP interface every relay of AXT offers.
info.description: The requests, responses, status codes and headers of a relay, as spec/transports.md, section 5, defines them; that section says what a relay and an app do with them. The paths are appended to the relay's base URL (section 5.2). Limits are named by their keys in types/axt/limits.json. A relay MUST NOT require cookies or any header that this document does not name, and an app MUST NOT send cookies. Only the list and the fetch have a body in their response; an app ignores the body of every other response.

servers.description: The relay's base URL without its last `/`: an absolute URL with the scheme https, a host and a path, of at most `transports.relay_url` bytes with that `/` (spec/transports.md, section 5.2).

put.description: The owner creates its mailbox before it gives the id to any other app, and again whenever an owner request gets 404 for the mailbox itself (section 5.4). Creating a mailbox that exists changes nothing.

201.description: A new mailbox. No body; an app ignores any body.

204.description: The mailbox exists already; nothing changed.

delete.description: Deletes the mailbox with its messages (section 5.8).

204.description: The mailbox and its messages are gone.

get.description: With `wait` from 1 to `transports.list_wait` (types/axt/limits.json) and no message in the mailbox, the relay holds the response for up to that many seconds until a message is put, and MAY answer sooner; without `wait`, or with 0, it answers at once (section 5.4).

200.description: The messages held, oldest put first.

put.description: Anyone who knows the mailbox id puts a sealed message (spec/keys.md, section 4.3). The relay checks in this order: `Content-Length` is present (411) and at most `transports.sealed_message` (413), before it reads the body; the mailbox exists (404); the body is not empty and its SHA-256 is `{message}` (400); it holds the message already (204, and nothing changes); the mailbox has room (507). It then holds the message (201). A put is safe to repeat (section 5.3).

parameters.name: Content-Length
parameters.description: The length of the sealed message in bytes.

201.description: The relay holds the message now.

204.description: The relay held the message already; nothing changed, also not its holding time.

get.description: The owner fetches each listed message, opens it, processes it and then deletes it (section 5.4).

200.description: The sealed message as it was put.

delete.description: The owner deletes a message after it has processed it, and a message that does not open as well (section 5.4).

204.description: The message is gone, also for a message the relay does not hold.

owner.description: The owner of the mailbox: `Authorization` with `Bearer`, one space and the mailbox secret as 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits (RFC 6750, section 2.1). The mailbox id is the SHA-256 of the ASCII text `AXT-v1 mailbox`, one zero byte and the 32 bytes of the secret (section 5.1).

message.name: message
message.description: The SHA-256 of the sealed message.

wait.name: wait
wait.description: Seconds to wait for a message, 0 to `transports.list_wait` (types/axt/limits.json); the only query of the interface.

RetryAfter.description: The seconds the app waits before it repeats the request.

BadRequest.description: A put whose body is empty or whose SHA-256 is not `{message}`; a `wait` that is not 0 to `transports.list_wait` (types/axt/limits.json); a query on another request. The app does not repeat the request: it is a fault of the app.

Unauthorized.description: An owner request without `Authorization`, or with one that is not `Bearer`, one space and a secret of 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits. The app does not repeat the request.

Forbidden.description: An owner request whose secret is not the mailbox's; for a creation also a mailbox the relay does not create for this app (spec/transports.md, section 5.6). The app does not repeat the request.

NotFound.description: A mailbox that does not exist, or a message the mailbox does not hold. After a put the app stops putting into the mailbox (section 5.3); the owner creates its mailbox again (section 5.4).

LengthRequired.description: A put without `Content-Length`. The app sends `Content-Length`.

ContentTooLarge.description: A put whose `Content-Length` is above `transports.sealed_message` (types/axt/limits.json), answered before the body is read (section 5.6). The app does not repeat the request.

TooManyRequests.description: A request above the relay's rate limits (section 5.6). The app waits as `Retry-After` says, then repeats it.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The relay cannot serve the request now. The app waits as `Retry-After` says, or without it as section 5.3 says, then repeats it.

InsufficientStorage.description: A put into a mailbox that has no room (section 5.6). The app waits as section 5.3 says, then repeats it.

List.description: An app ignores members it does not know.

messages.description: The messages held, oldest put first, at most `transports.list_messages` (types/axt/limits.json).

items.description: One message held; an app ignores members it does not know.
